figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of SPD-MetaFormer. (a) Convolutional features yield local covariance memories (blue) and an observed summary (green), embedded in a common SPD space. After the SPD block, a geometric readout with learned weights shared across trials (dotted spokes) pools all tokens for tangent-space classification. (b) The attention-free block updates only the summary through uniform geometric memory aggregation and a gated geodesic residual, then applies shared spectral shrinkage to every token. Circles, diamonds, and stars denote memories, the summary, and Fréchet means, respectively.
Table 1: Comparison with published EEG results. MI and SSVEP report accuracy (%); ERN reports AUC (%). Baseline entries are reproduced from Table 3 of Jin et al. (2026).

Table 4: Training with learned versus locked-uniform weights in existing MAtt and GBWAtt reproductions. Values are mean ± mean within-subject run SD (sample SD over ten runs per subject, averaged over subjects); ∆ is uniform minus learned, with a paired subject-bootstrap 95% interval. All scores are multiplied by 100. GBWAtt comparisons match θ = 1.5 on both sides. These experiments use their own matched reproduction protocols (Appendix A.5).

Table 5: Attention entropy at the validation-selected checkpoint, averaged over test queries/trials, then seeds and subjects. SD(H) averages the within-subject sample SD over ten runs. Natural logarithms give nats. Uniform weights have H = logm and H/ logm = 1 exactly. GBWAtt uses θ = 1.5.
Table 6: Dataset-specific SPD-MetaFormer frontend. Cin → Cout denotes convolutional feature channels, with kernel sizes shown in parentheses.
Table 7: Fixed training recipes for SPD-MetaFormer and its paired ablations.

Table 9: Temperature controls with three seeds. Default uses τ = 1; tuned and learnable settings are selected by validation loss. Scores are accuracy (MI/SSVEP) or AUC (ERN), multiplied by 100. ∆ is tuned minus uniform, with a paired subject-bootstrap 95% interval.

Figure 2: Temperature, predictive performance, and allocation entropy after full retraining. Top: mean test scores with the within-subject sample SD over three runs, averaged over subjects; dashed lines show each model’s retrained uniform control. Scores are accuracy (MI/SSVEP) or AUC (ERN), multiplied by 100, with separate vertical scales across datasets. Bottom: normalized attention entropy, where one denotes uniform allocation. All points average three seeds within subjects.
Table 10: ABIDE-I (CC200) test performance: mean ± population SD (×100) over ten shared subject splits (seeds 0–9). SPD-MetaFormer and MAtt use d = 32. Bold marks the largest mean in each column.

Figure 4: Contribution of the spectral FFN across token granularities. Top: accuracy (MI/SSVEP) or AUC (ERN), ×100, with the within-subject sample SD over ten runs, averaged over subjects. Bottom: FFN gain with subject-bootstrap 95% intervals; filled markers indicate intervals excluding zero. Ten seeds are averaged within each subject. Dotted lines mark the main-model settings; these single-threaded reruns differ from Table 1 by at most 0.11 points.
